primary.title: Dhammapada
primary.author: Gautama Buddha
primary.rationale: A collection of sayings and teachings attributed to Gautama Buddha, considered a foundational text in Buddhism.

primary.title: Sutta Nipata
primary.author: Gautama Buddha
primary.rationale: A collection of ancient Buddhist scriptures, containing verses attributed to the Buddha, covering various ethical and philosophical topics.

primary.title: Majjhima Nikaya
primary.author: Gautama Buddha
primary.rationale: A collection of the Buddha's middle-length discourses, offering insights into his teachings on various aspects of the path to enlightenment.

secondary.title: The Buddha and His Dhamma
secondary.author: B. R. Ambedkar
secondary.rationale: While published slightly before 1976, this is a seminal work by a prominent scholar reinterpreting Buddhist teachings and the life of the Buddha from a modern, critical perspective. It is widely available and influential.

secondary.title: What the Buddha Taught
secondary.author: Walpola Rahula
secondary.rationale: Another foundational text for understanding Buddhist doctrine, offering a clear and accessible explanation of the Buddha's core teachings. Though slightly before 1976, it remains a standard scholarly introduction.

secondary.title: The Life of the Buddha: As Told by His Disciples
secondary.author: Bhikkhu Nanamoli
secondary.rationale: This scholarly work reconstructs the life of the Buddha based on early Buddhist texts, providing a critical and detailed historical account.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources attributed to Gautama Buddha are generally collections of his discourses and sayings, compiled by his disciples. Exact dating is challenging, but they are considered to represent his teachings. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly rigor and accessibility in understanding the historical and philosophical context of the Buddha's life and teachings.
